newsitem.title: USA: Saudi deal for U.S. F-16 fighters called premature.
newsitem.headline: Saudi deal for U.S. F-16 fighters called premature.

text.p: U.S. officials and Lockheed Martin Corp. on Thursday termed premature a published report that Saudi Arabia had agreed to buy up to 100 Lockheed F-16 fighter jets in a multibillion-dollar deal.

The Washington Times said on Thursday that Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan was expected to bring a request for the sale to Washington next month in the latest in a string of U.S. arms deals with the wealthy Gulf kingdom.

The Times said the step to replace ageing U.S.-built F-5 jets in the Saudi arsenal could be worth $30 billion, but industry officials said flyaway costs of each F-16 were $25 million, making such a deal worth at least $2.5 billion not including maintenance and costly air-to-air missiles.

"There is a lot of enthusiasm in a lot of places for the idea, but we have received no official request or contract for that kind of sale from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

"The report is premature," Norman Robbins, a spokesman for Lockheed's tactical aircraft division in Fort Worth, Texas, told Reuters. He said talks had been under way but stressed that any deal would have to be approved by the two governments.

Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon also said no formal request had been received from the Saudis, although other U.S. officials said Lockheed had been actively discussing a deal with the Saudis for some time.

A White House official who asked not to be identified said he could neither confirm or deny that a new fighter deal was in the works. "The story has bubbled up before and nothing came of it. It may or may not be true this time," he said.
The Saudis have bought 114 older F-5 jets from the United States in past years and also are flying 98 more advanced F-15 C and D model fighters built by McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Saudi Arabia bought an additional 72 advanced F-15S model ground attack jets from McDonnell in 1994 for $9.2 billion and have now taken delivery of 17 of those, according to U.S. Air Force officials.
A new sale of fighter jets to the Saudis would come at a time of tension between Washington and Riyadh over two bombings in Saudi Arabia in a little over a year that have killed 24 Americans.

FBI and U.S. Justice Department officials this month accused the Saudis of a lack of full cooperation in a joint investigation of the truck bombing of a military housing complex in Dhahran last June 25 that killed 19 U.S. troops.
Five other Americans died in a bombing at a Saudi National Guard facility in Riyadh in late 1995.
